relevance_note: One cohort member carries a TNFAIP3 variant: '1 TNFAIP3 mutation (A20 haploinsufficiency, #15 with BD)'; his mother also carries it.
method_note: Read the whole paper; wrote the JSON with a Python script in my scratch directory. Every table span was cut from the actual Table 1 / Table 2 row text for #15 (so it is character-exact) and every span was checked verbatim by script; transcription of the two #15 rows was checked by eye against the tables. Patients are rows in both tables. SCOPE: this is a 15-patient cohort (recurrent aphthous stomatitis with systemic inflammation); only patient #15 carries a TNFAIP3 variant. I extracted #15 and his two relatives (the mother, who carries the A20 mutation and has BD, and the grandmother, who has BD-like complaints). The other 14 enrolled patients (STAT1 #1, #10; PTPN22 #2; DNASE1L3 #5; genetic-negative others) and their relatives in the family-history column were NOT extracted, because they have no TNFAIP3 variant; the instructions leave non-TNFAIP3 papers' tables empty, and I applied the same scope within this mixed cohort. Revisit if the harness expects all cohort members. Age at last evaluation '16' is Table 1's 'Age at enrollment (y)'; follow-up continued after that (6 months on adalimumab), so it is the age at enrollment, not strictly the last evaluation. Onset '0.3' (y) given as P0.3Y without converting to months. Transcript NM_001270508 (no version) is printed in Methods for TNFAIP3, and the Table 2 legend says the variant column refers to the Methods transcript. cDNA is printed in non-standard form 'c.C1135T'; recorded as printed. Authors do not name the variant class (only 'p.Q379X'), so variant_type is 'not reported'. Table 2 'Inheritance' column ('AD') is the mode of inheritance, not variant origin; origin 'inherited maternal' comes from 'STATUS (carrier) HZ(mother)' and the text. Mother's zygosity left 'not reported' because 'HZ' describes the patient. No functional assay was done for the TNFAIP3 variant: only in silico predictions (GERP 5.63, CADD 39, LRT D, MT D; SIFT/PP2 na) and the patient-level IFN score. Grandmother: carrier status not stated; 'nephew' is the paper's word for her grandson #15; maternal or paternal side not stated. BD was not entered as a phenotypic feature (it is a diagnosis; recorded in disease_label_as_stated). HLA-B51 negative not entered as a phenotype. 'usually normal CRP' was entered as excluded with the qualifier 'usually'. GI checklist item marked observed from 'perianal ulcerations' and 'Fecal calprotectin ↑' (judgement call). IBD excluded for #15 from the explicit cohort-wide statement 'we did not identify any patient with RAS and inflammatory bowel disease' (evidence_basis inferred from group statement); this narrower absence does not change the GI checklist item. Contradictions/oddities in the paper (none change #15's data): patient #1 is 'F' in Table 1 but 'he' in the text; patient #5's DNASE1L3 variant is 'T971fs*2' in Table 1 vs 'p.T97Ifs*2' in Table 2; the IFN-score paragraph cites Table 2, but IFN scores are in Table 1; 'PEDDB' vs 'PEDBD'; the abstract says the TNFAIP3 mutation was 'in patients with BD' (plural) while the Results give one patient (#15).
